prerequisites: Proficient handling of mathematical tools including trigonometry, analytical geometry, functions of several variables, two and three-dimensional integration, and linear differential equations.
Having passed and maintaining a good level of knowledge in 'Teoría de Máquinas' (Theory of Machines), especially the Dynamics part.
Elementary knowledge in programming or the use of spreadsheets.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and skills to apply the scientific and technological fundamentals of dynamic machine analysis.

teaching_methods: Distance learning (UNED methodology) via a virtual course.
Theoretical approaches followed by practical applications, exercises, and problems.
Detailed reading of the Study Guide and progressive study of the basic text chapters.
Problem-solving practice and completion of proposed activities, including distance evaluation tests (PECs) involving spreadsheets.
assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as 0.8 * In-person Exam Grade + 0.4 * Continuous Assessment Grade. The Continuous Assessment grade is only considered if at least 4 points are achieved in the in-person exam. To pass without Continuous Assessment, a minimum of 6 points is required in the in-person exam. If Continuous Assessment is completed, a minimum of 4 points in the in-person exam is sufficient to pass. Continuous assessment tests can be submitted or resubmitted before September 1st for the extraordinary call.
